analysis.summary: Kevin revisited the proposal with Rachel (COO) during the negotiation stage. Rachel raised pricing and implementation concerns; Kevin acknowledged these, mentioned product capabilities and onboarding support, and agreed to send a revised proposal with an ROI breakdown for Rachel to review internally.
analysis.next_steps: Rep will send a revised proposal with pricing options and an ROI breakdown plus a detailed implementation plan; customer will review internally.
strengths: Acknowledged and validated the customer's pricing concern rather than dismissing it.
Offered concrete next steps by committing to a revised proposal and ROI breakdown.
Raised onboarding support to address implementation complexity, signaling available services.
Kept the call concise and obtained agreement for the customer to review the follow-up materials.
areas_for_improvement: Ask open-ended discovery questions to uncover budget constraints, decision criteria, and who else is involved in the decision.
Probe the competitor situation: ask which competitor, what features/pricing they offer, and why the customer is comparing them.
Quantify value on the call (potential ROI, time saved, cost offsets) instead of relying on a later document to justify premium pricing.
Avoid early product statements; tie any product benefits directly to the specific pains Rachel raised.
Secure a firm follow-up meeting time and participants rather than only sending materials to be reviewed internally.
action_items: Send a revised proposal reflecting any possible pricing adjustments and clearly documented options/tiers.
Include a tailored ROI breakdown with assumptions and metrics relevant to Rachel's operations.
Attach a detailed implementation/onboarding plan with timeline, milestones, and assigned resources.
Request the competitor name and a feature/price comparison to address gaps directly in the proposal.
Propose a scheduled follow-up meeting (date/time) to review the revised proposal with key stakeholders.
objections_raised: Pricing is a sticking point / premium price is not justified

Reinforced value by mentioning advanced analytics and automation capabilities.

Probe the implementation concerns in detail (specific pain points, past experiences, required integrations) instead of giving a high-level reassurance.
